title: Find Smallest Letter Greater Than Target
summary: Given an array of characters that is sorted in non-decreasing order and a target character, find the smallest character in the array that is lexicographically greater than the target.
statement: Given an array of characters that is sorted in non-decreasing order and a target character, find the smallest character in the array that is lexicographically greater than the target. If no such character exists, return the first character in the array.
constraints: Letters are sorted and contain at least two distinct lowercase characters.
Return the smallest letter strictly greater than target, wrapping to the first letter.
reference_solution:
def next_greater_letter(letters, target):
    left,right=0,len(letters)
    while left<right:
        middle=(left+right)//2
        if letters[middle]<=target:left=middle+1
        else:right=middle
    return letters[left%len(letters)]

def next_greater_letter(letters, target):
    left,right=0,len(letters)
    while left<right:
        middle=(left+right)//2
        if letters[middle]<=target:left=middle+1
        else:right=middle
    return letters[min(left,len(letters)-1)]

Move left past values <= target; return letters[left modulo length].
The search invariant partitions all rejected values from all strict candidates, while modulo implements the required wrap.
